title: Input.state is unwired in the camera-input fixture: the app/input test suite segfaults (CI input leg red)
evidence:
cam_test_ctx wires only:
	ictx.topo = &st.topology
	ictx.cat = cat
	ictx.log = log
(no `ictx.state = &st`), while commit_draw now dereferences it:
		if _, err := pp.box_apply_edit(inp.state, pp.Command{1, cmd}, inp.cat); err == .None {
Reproduced: `odin test app/input` -> "Finished 13 tests in 2.916ms. 1 test failed." / " - input.draw_drag_on_a_node_never_pans 	Signal caught: Segmentation_Fault"
detail: The diff added state:^Run_State to Input and routed commit_draw through box_apply_edit, but patched only exec_test's fixtures; cam_test_ctx's real draw gesture hits the nil pointer. CI's `odin test app/input` leg is red; pullback_test.odin:241 is the same latent unwired site.
recommended_fix: Wire `ictx.state = &st` in cam_test_ctx and pullback_test's input wiring (or make box_apply_edit nil-tolerant as a pure delegate); re-run `odin test app/input` green.

title: Placement refusals are silently swallowed: the Box's teaching "no" exists only on the draw path
detail: Ruling 4's "only tiers you hold" is the biggest behavioral change, yet a refused placement is invisible: no toast (label wired but unreachable), and the ghost previews a topology-valid spot. Inconsistent with the diff's own draw-path teaching contract.
recommended_fix: Add the last_reject/reject_tick else-branch to Place_Release and include the box material check in the placement ghost's validation so an empty tier previews as unaffordable.

title: stats_destroy never frees rec.box.pieces — one leaked dynamic array per stepped tick on box-on stats runs
detail: stats_destroy is the record's ODN-18 owner ("free the record's owned buffers") and callers destroy per tick (harness/run.odin:485,936; app/main.odin:594,965), so every box-on tick with stats emission leaks the pieces array. Breaks the file's own destroy discipline.
recommended_fix: Add `delete(rec.box.pieces)` to stats_destroy; run a --stats-out box-on pass under leak checking to confirm.

title: box_validate re-implements apply_demolish_node's incident-pipe rule — refund correctness is bound to topology internals by comment only
detail: The refund depends on exactly which pipes apply_demolish_node tombstones; nothing but a comment ("the same scan apply_demolish_node uses") enforces lockstep. A topology-side change to the batch rule silently corrupts refunds — breaking the full-refund ruling invisibly.
recommended_fix: Share one topology-owned incident-pipe scan/manifest (e.g., apply_demolish_node reports destroyed tier/spans, or a common helper both call) so the refund cannot drift from the destruction.

title: The crisis-stall scenario exercises no crisis — the Q7 "prove with a sim run" mandate is named, not tested
detail: The scenario is era3-slope with seed 7: it neither forces nor measures a crisis, so it cannot evidence "crisis drops deliveries -> dots slow -> floor absorbs it". The [floor,base] clamp holds structurally, but the record's mandated sim proof is unexercised.
recommended_fix: Force a crisis (or drive the zero-delivery window one causes), count crisis events in Econ_Stats, and assert stock recovery across dots during the stall — or rename the scenario to what it actually measures.

title: Cmd_Era_Advance validate+latch block duplicated verbatim in both box_apply_edit branches
evidence:
Both the disabled branch:
		case Cmd_Era_Advance:
			if e := era_advance_validate(state, c, cat); e != .None {
				return {}, e
			}
			era_advance_latch(state, c)
			return {}, .None
and the enabled branch carry the identical case:
	case Cmd_Era_Advance:
		if e := era_advance_validate(state, c, cat); e != .None {
			return {}, e
		}
		era_advance_latch(state, c)
		return {}, .None
detail: The advance spends no material and box_validate ignores it, so the two copies can be hoisted above the box_enabled check — removing a drift hazard where one copy gains a guard the other lacks.
recommended_fix: Handle Cmd_Era_Advance once at the top of box_apply_edit (validate, latch, return) before the box_enabled branch.

title: Router short-name mapping duplicated between draw_box_hud and draw_tray
evidence:
draw_box_hud (2424) and draw_tray (2479) both carry:
		if short == "router_basic" { short = "basic" } else if short == "router_mid" { short = "mid" } else if short == "router_high" { short = "high" }
detail: The id->chip-label map now lives in two HUD sites; a new router tier must be added in both or the tray and the box line disagree. Small debt, cheap to fold.
recommended_fix: Extract a router_short_name(nt: Node_Type) -> string helper used by both draw sites.
